analysis.title: Market and Liquidity Update 11.18.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 was up 0.30% premarket on 11/18 and rates were +/- 1bp, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.10%.
Yesterday (11/17) Treasury yields fell 2-3bps across the curve as risk-off drove a flight to quality, despite firmer retail sales data.
Tech was weak again, with the Nasdaq 100 re-testing its local lows ahead of the NVDA earnings report.

Rich Privorotsky (GS Head of European One Delta Trading) said NVDA beat and raised, guiding to $130bn against roughly $125bn expected, with zero China data centre compute in the numbers. He added that the spending isn't stopping, and that the market would have liked a hint that Jensen could come back but the company shut that down.

The GS rates desk says tactical demand for Treasuries is improving, although yesterday's long-end buyback was far weaker than expected: only 20% of announced capacity was used ($1.18bn accepted), against the full $6bn taken in the previous operation.
Mortgage-backed securities reversed late on 11/17, moving from 1 tick wider to 2.5-3 ticks tighter between 3pm and 5pm. The initial widening matched the drop in risk from the tech outages.

Hedge funds and some asset managers bought more heavily to lift the mortgage basis into the close. Flows after the NVDA print were muted, though the basis gapped about 1-1.5 ticks tighter after 4:30pm.

Within the mortgage stack, lower coupons lagged on better selling, outright and via coupon swaps, and ended 1-1.5 ticks wider. The rest of the stack ended 2-3 ticks tighter. Origination was light at about $1.3bn.
FOMC minutes are due at 2pm on 11/18. The GS economics team will look for the assumptions behind participants' economic outlooks and their views on the balance of risks at the time.
GS Economics: October core retail sales rose 0.6%, above expectations, and the retail sales level was revised up sharply. Q4 GDP tracking rose to +2.4%, and GS estimates October core PCE at 0.29%.
GS Economics: October industrial production fell 0.4%, below expectations, mostly on a decline in utilities, which is source data for consumption in GDP.
GS Economics forecasts Italian real GDP growth of 0.5% in 2027, below consensus, on weaker consumption and slowing investment.

GS Equity Research midday note (11/17): the S&P 500 is down 3% for the week as investors reassess the AI trade alongside peaking earnings, potentially peak AI investment and a tightening Fed. The S&P has already lost 4 turns off its P/E peak from earlier this year.
GS Equity Research: Asia stocks fell on 11/17 after the almost 2% S&P 500 sell-off on 11/16, amid uncertainty over US chip supply in China (US BIS remote-access rule).
